exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
cohort: A total of 351 women who had recently given birth (vaginal or cesarean delivery) and completed questionnaires over the first postpartum year.
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased prevalence of depressive symptoms at 3 months and higher pain levels that persisted at 6 months postpartum.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery also resulted in lower perineal pain immediately postpartum but higher sexual desire and lower sexual satisfaction at 4-6 weeks, with no lasting differences in sexual function after 6 weeks or in depressive symptom trends within one year.
